note: Trophy Atlas route, steps and dossier copy freshly authored for this variant around the official 55-trophy list. Hours, difficulty ratings, prerequisites and scenario interpretations are the author's own estimates; the in-game trackers are the authority on every count.

phases.name: Green Light
phases.goal: Clear the opening mission and take full control of Leonida.
phases.about: The route starts where the story starts. Nothing else on the list is reachable before the opening mission is done, so this short phase exists to get every player onto the same page.

phases.name: Story Run: Chapters 1-3
phases.goal: Push the campaign through the first three chapters.
phases.about: A straight march down the main mission markers. Required missions that fall inside this stretch are collected here so the story route stays a single, uninterrupted line of work.

phases.name: Story Run: Chapter 4 & Finale
phases.goal: Finish the last numbered chapter and the closing mission.
phases.about: The story ends here, and with it every mission-type trophy on the list. Keep optional work on hold; the atlas deliberately leaves the open-world sweep for after the credits.

phases.name: Street Work & Heists
phases.goal: Work the crime loop: robberies, heists, heat and odd stunts.
phases.about: With the story tools in hand, the crime economy is fully open. This phase batches every robbery, wanted-level stunt and vehicle oddity so the money and the mischief share one block of play.

phases.name: Stranger Strands
phases.goal: Close out the named stranger strands and their odd moments.
phases.about: Each strand is a short campaign of its own. Running them as one phase keeps the map logic coherent and feeds both the strand-count trophy and the strange-moment unlocks at the same time.

phases.name: Activities & Skill Checks
phases.goal: Clear the volume and skill trophies: stunts, races, ranges and challenges.
phases.about: The largest pure-playtime block. These are repeatable systems rather than one-off scenes, so they can be paced across as many sessions as the totals demand.

phases.name: Collections, Property & Completion
phases.goal: Sweep the world and close the 100% completion stat.
phases.about: The long tail. Collections, property, one-off scenes and the completion stat itself live here, and the atlas treats them as the final audit rather than a background task.

phases.name: The Platinum Stamp
phases.goal: Confirm nothing is left, then collect the platinum.
phases.about: No work remains by design. This phase is the audit step: reconcile every counter, then let the last unlock hand over the platinum.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This platinum is not a task; it is the receipt for the other fifty-four. The atlas route is built so that the final item you tick is always a real trophy, and this one lands in the same notification stack seconds later. Resist the urge to hunt it directly — it cannot be earned early, traded or rushed. Keep a clean checklist through the endgame and it simply arrives.
steps: Complete all fifty-four other trophies
Reconcile the in-game counters one last time
Accept the platinum on the final unlock
trophies.hint: Nothing to do here except finish everything else.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: it is the automatic capstone of a complete list. The only failure mode is stopping before the fifty-fourth unlock.
trophies.verification: Open the console trophy list and confirm every other entry shows earned before treating the route as finished.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing sits at the front door of the campaign, so the trophy arrives minutes into a fresh save. Play its objectives in order and let the closing scenes run before you touch anything else. There is no hidden condition in the official wording. Every route to the platinum passes through here within the first sitting.
steps: Start a new campaign
Play the opening mission through its objectives
Let the closing scene finish before stopping
trophies.hint: It is the very first thing the game asks of you.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: the opening mission cannot be skipped, and the unlock follows its completion directly.
trophies.verification: The trophy notification appears at the mission-end scene; the console list records it immediately.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter one ends when its last scene rolls, and that moment is the whole trophy. Keep to the main mission line and avoid abandoning a mission midway, since the conservative habit is to always complete what you start. Nothing optional is required by the description. Treat it as a free tick on the story march.
steps: Play the chapter one missions in order
Complete the chapter closing scene
Check the unlock on the notification
trophies.hint: Follow the main markers; the chapter end is the trigger.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: chapter trophies track the story itself. The only caution is not to leave a chapter mission half-done at a session break.
trophies.verification: The chapter transition screen doubles as the unlock moment; the trophy list confirms it.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: The second chapter is another milestone on the same straight road: finish its missions, let the closing scene play, collect the trophy. The official wording attaches no side condition, so optional content can wait. Its colorful name is a reference to the money theme of the stretch, not a task. Keep the story momentum and this one costs nothing extra.
steps: Continue the story into chapter two
Finish every mission the chapter presents
Watch for the unlock at the chapter close
trophies.hint: The second chapter ends where the trophy fires.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified, for the same reason as the other chapter trophies. Play each mission through rather than quitting mid-objective.
trophies.verification: Unlock fires at the chapter two ending; the console trophy list is the record.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Chapter three carries the story into Vice City proper by its name, and the trophy lands when the chapter closes. There is nothing to grind and nothing to choose; the requirement is plain completion. As with all chapter trophies, the atlas advice is to never abandon a running mission at the midpoint. The unlock should be one of the most reliable on the list.
steps: Progress the story into chapter three
Complete the chapter’s missions
Let the ending scene run to the unlock
trophies.hint: The third chapter’s closing scene is the unlock.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: it follows the chapter end directly. Completing offered missions rather than skipping them is the only stated-relevant habit.
trophies.verification: Chapter transition plus notification; confirm in the trophy list afterwards.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter four is the last numbered chapter before the endgame, and the trophy fires when it closes. Nothing in the description asks for optional work, so keep the run lean. The atlas places a planning note here: this is a sensible moment to decide when your collection sweep will happen, since the world stays open afterwards. The unlock itself is automatic on chapter completion.
steps: Play through chapter four
Finish the chapter’s final scene
Consider this the cue to plan the open-world sweep
trophies.hint: The fourth chapter’s end scene is the unlock.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: it unlocks with the chapter. Whether the finale blocks backtracking is unverified, so finish optional strands before the credits if you prefer caution.
trophies.verification: Unlock at the chapter four ending; the trophy list confirms.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission is the story’s last gate, and plain completion is all the official wording asks. Expect a longer set-piece than a routine chapter mission, which is why the atlas rates it slightly above the chapter ticks. No medal or performance threshold is mentioned. Save your resources for it and treat the ending scenes as part of the mission.
steps: Reach the closing mission of the story
Complete all of its objectives
Collect the gold unlock at the mission end
trophies.hint: One mission: the last one in the story.
trophies.missable: Treat the risk as negligible but real: required missions normally stay reachable after the credits, yet replay behavior is not verified. Do not deliberately postpone it to the very end of the platinum without reason.
trophies.verification: The mission-end notification; the gold entry appears in the console list immediately.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a required story mission, which means no route can avoid it and no extra preparation is needed. Start it from the mission flow, complete each objective, and finish the end scene. The official wording sets no performance bar. It is an automatic tick for anyone following the chapters in order.
steps: Reach Breakfast Run in the mission flow
Complete its objective list
Let the mission end screen settle
trophies.hint: A required early mission; the flow delivers it.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: required missions are expected to be completable on any playthrough. Retry behavior is assumed from series convention, not verified.
trophies.verification: Mission-end notification; the trophy list confirms the entry.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a required mission and completion alone is the requirement. Heist-style missions often offer approach choices, and nothing in the description rewards one over another, so pick the plan that suits your style. Play it through in one sitting if you can; abandoning mid-heist risks losing setup progress. The trophy lands at the mission end.
steps: Start The Cartel Heist from the story
Play the setup and execution objectives
Finish the mission rather than abandoning it
trophies.hint: The cartel heist plays out through the story flow.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified for a completed playthrough. Whether failed attempts require a full restart is unverified, so finish what you start.
trophies.verification: Notification at mission end; check the trophy list entry.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child’s Play is a required mission somewhere in the mid-story, and the atlas leaves its exact placement to the game’s own flow rather than guessing a chapter. Completion is the whole requirement. Play it through, watch the ending, and move on. No optional condition is attached in the official wording.
steps: Continue the story until Child’s Play appears
Complete the mission objectives
Let the closing scene run
trophies.hint: A story mission; the flow decides when.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: it is a required mission. Its placement in the chapter order is an estimate in this guide, not a verified fact.
trophies.verification: Mission-end notification; the trophy list confirms.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is another required mission, so the story itself schedules it. Completion is the only condition the official wording states. Avoid retry loops for style; a clean finished run is all the trophy wants. The unlock arrives at the mission end like the rest of this set.
steps: Reach Headliners in the story flow
Complete all objectives in one run
Collect the unlock at the end screen
trophies.hint: One more required mission on the story line.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: required missions are assumed fully completable. Retry behavior remains a convention-based assumption.
trophies.verification: Notification at mission end; trophy list confirms.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown takes the story to the airport authority, and completing it is the entire trophy. Expect a set-piece pace rather than a stealth exercise. Note for later planning: the free-roam airport stunt in the street phase is a different trophy, so do not conflate the two locations. The unlock is automatic at mission end.
steps: Play VCIA Takedown from the story flow
Complete its objectives in order
Finish the closing scene
trophies.hint: The airport-themed story mission.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: it is required content. Its chapter placement is an estimate of this atlas, not a verified fact.
trophies.verification: Mission-end notification; the trophy list shows the entry.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory sounds like a set-piece operation, and its trophy is plain completion of it. Budget a longer session than for a routine mission, since operations of this name tend to run multi-stage. No performance threshold appears in the description. Finish the end scene and the tick is yours.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story
Work through the full objective list
Collect the unlock after the end scene
trophies.hint: A late-story operation mission; expect a long one.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: required content. Length is the only notable cost, and that is an estimate from the name.
trophies.verification: Unlock at the mission end; trophy list confirms.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: One hundred percent completion is the heaviest single item in this atlas, and it deserves to be treated as a project rather than a trophy. The official wording does not enumerate what counts, so the in-game checklist is the only authority worth trusting. The atlas advice is to audit the tracker early, schedule its categories as their own sessions, and re-check after every batch of content. Nothing about it is missable in the usual sense; the real risk is an unknown requirement discovered late.
steps: Open the in-game completion checklist early
Clear its categories region by region
Re-audit after each batch and before the platinum push
trophies.hint: The in-game completion stat is the authority; audit it region by region.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified in the usual sense, because it is a running stat. The practical danger is an unlisted checklist item, so cross-check the in-game tracker early and often.
trophies.verification: The in-game completion percentage reaching 100 is the proof; the unlock notification follows it.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty stunts is a volume figure, and the description reads it as a cumulative count rather than a set of specific jumps. The atlas habit is simple: never drive anywhere without hunting a ramp, a hill or a drift line, because the count climbs invisibly while you do everything else. Save a deliberate stunt loop in a fast car for the final stretch, when the last dozens refuse to arrive. A single long evening usually closes it.
steps: Chain stunts on every drive between objectives
Favor obvious ramps, hills and drift opportunities
Close the last dozens with a dedicated fast-car loop
trophies.hint: Every ramp and drift adds to the running total.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: the count is cumulative and stunts presumably stay available after the story. What exactly qualifies as a stunt is unverified, so favor the obvious actions.
trophies.verification: Watch the running total in the relevant stats screen; the unlock notification fires at 250.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The description asks you to try each type of activity once, and the atlas treats the in-game activity menu as the definitive type list since no count is stated officially. The trick of this trophy is breadth, not skill: a single entered session of each type satisfies the wording. Sampling during the story keeps it nearly free. Do a final menu audit before writing it off.
steps: List the activity types from the in-game menu
Enter one session of each type
Cross-check the menu for any type you missed
trophies.hint: Open every kind of activity once, even briefly.
trophies.missable: Treat as borderline only because an unknown activity type could be overlooked; activities are presumably always open. The menu audit is the safeguard.
trophies.verification: No stated counter; confirm by your own menu walkthrough that each type has been opened.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold in every Shooting Range challenge is a skill trophy, and the atlas advises learning before scoring: several drills reward rhythm and target order over raw reaction speed. Settle your loadout and settings first, then climb the list one challenge at a time. This is one of the harder items on the list and deserves multiple focused sessions. The range is a repeatable system, so a lost evening costs nothing but time.
steps: Learn each range challenge type with practice runs
Then chase gold one challenge at a time
Budget several sessions rather than one marathon
trophies.hint: Practice each drill before chasing the gold threshold.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: the range is repeatable and medals presumably persist. Whether an existing medal can be re-earned for a better score is unverified, but it does not affect the trophy.
trophies.verification: The range results screens show the medal per challenge; the unlock fires when all show gold.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: A win at every Top Fun location is a tour with a competitive twist: finishing is not enough, first place is. The atlas method is to use the first entry at a new location as a scouting lap, then push for the win once the shortcuts are known. Treat the in-game location list as the checklist rather than trusting memory. A win at the last location closes the trophy.
steps: Enter a Top Fun race at each location once to learn it
Learn each course’s shortcuts early
Convert every location into a first-place finish
trophies.hint: Win, not just finish, at each drone race location.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: races are repeatable activities. The location count is whatever the in-game menu lists; this guide does not state a number as fact.
trophies.verification: Each location shows your best result in its menu entry; the unlock follows the last first-place.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different races means twenty distinct events, not twenty wins of one favorite. The atlas advice is to diversify from the start: rotate across the race categories and locations, keeping a rough tally as you go. Repeat wins of the same event presumably add nothing, so a farmed circuit is wasted effort. Race pacing matters more than speed here.
steps: Spread entries across the race types offered
Count wins against distinct events, not repeats
Convert a sure lead carefully in the final laps
trophies.hint: Twenty distinct wins; variety beats farming.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: races repeat. Whether wins from different categories all count is unverified; the plain reading is any twenty distinct race events.
trophies.verification: Track distinct wins yourself and watch for the notification on the twentieth.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beating Cal is a single rivalry duel inside the fishing activity, not a fishing grind. Learn what the duel measures, size or count, then outperform him by it. If a first attempt falls short, the activity format implies a retry, though that is convention rather than verified fact. One comfortable evening is a generous budget.
steps: Find the fishing challenge through the fishing activity
Learn the duel’s scoring measure
Outperform Cal and take the win
trophies.hint: One named rival duel; win it once.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified, assuming the challenge can be re-attempted. The conservative move is to attempt it when your fishing handling feels solid.
trophies.verification: The duel result screen is the immediate proof; the notification follows the win.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: One completed arcade game is the whole requirement, so the atlas says to pick the cabinet you like best rather than sampling all of them. Play the game to its natural end and let the result screen settle. There is no score threshold in the description. This is a coffee-break trophy.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet through the arcade activity
Pick the game you find easiest
Play it to its natural end screen
trophies.hint: Any cabinet, any game, finished once.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: arcade cabinets are permanent fixtures. The description names no specific game.
trophies.verification: The game’s own end screen followed by the notification.

The atlas counts this strand as completion content too, so the time is never wasted. One or two free-roam sittings should cover the whole line.

Run the strand’s missions in sequence and keep the line in mind during free-roam sessions so it closes in a handful of sittings. The strand feeds the completion audit as well, which the atlas treats as a bonus. The unlock arrives at the final mission’s end.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.

The atlas prefers starting strands early in the free-roam phase so their steps spread across sessions instead of stacking at the end. Play the missions as the strand presents them. trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight completed strands is a commitment count, and the silver grade signals the scale. The atlas rule is simple: finish what you start, because a half-done strand is progress you cannot bank. There are more strands in the state than eight, so choose the lines that suit your route and close them one by one. Track the finished total in the pause menu before moving on.

trophies.verification: The pause-menu strand tracker shows completed strands; the unlock fires at eight.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy’s strand follows the same shape as its siblings: a line of missions closing in a final one, which is the trophy. Play it in order during the free-roam phase and it costs an evening at most. The strand also feeds the completion audit. The unlock arrives with the final mission.
steps: Start Randy’s strand

Run it like the rest: in order, at free-roam pace, with the strand tracker open. The named strands together also make the eight-strand count realistic, which is why this phase batches them. The final mission delivers the unlock.
steps: Start Tyrone’s strand
Play its missions in sequence
Close the final mission for the unlock
trophies.hint: Tyrone’s strand, in order, to the end.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: standard strand content. The in-strand order is convention, not verified.
trophies.verification: Strand list shows the final mission complete; notification follows.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditation at every spot is a map-sweep trophy, and the atlas treats the in-game markers as the definitive count since the official description states no number. Sweep region by region rather than chasing pins at random, and use each spot the moment you find it. The last few are always the ones you skipped, so a final map audit is part of the plan. Collectible-type content like this feeds the completion audit too.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret’s strand funnels into one unique animal hunt, and completing that hunt is the trophy. Take the strand’s earlier missions first, then approach the hunt on its own terms, since a unique hunt may carry clean-take conditions the description does not spell out. Patience is the whole skill here. The strand also feeds the stranger-strand work, so the effort is shared.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Three complete card sets is the classic collection loop, and the atlas insists on a checklist because a set with one missing card is worth zero. Gather cards region by region rather than at random, and reconcile each set’s gaps before moving to a new area. Sets are finite, so a missing card is recoverable only by finding it. The third completed set triggers the unlock.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: One hundred WAiNK locations is a traversal trophy, and the atlas plans it like a delivery route: dense districts first in passing, far corners in one dedicated session at the end. The in-game tracker shows the running total, which is the only number worth trusting. The last handful is always the slowest, so budget a final sweep. Keep moving; the counter does the rest.

Trigger the WAiNK action at each location
Save the far corners for a dedicated session
trophies.hint: Cover dense areas first, the far edges last.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: the locations are fixed world content. What exactly triggers a location’s count is whatever the in-game prompt indicates.
trophies.verification: The in-game counter shows the running total; the unlock fires at 100.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Fifty challenges is a volume target rather than a skill wall, and the atlas advises treating it as background work: a handful per session across the campaign reaches it without a dedicated grind. Sample every type you meet, finish what suits you, and let the tally grow. No specific challenge list is stated officially. The fiftieth completion fires the unlock.
steps: Sample every challenge type you encounter
Finish the ones that suit your build
Tally the completions across sessions
trophies.hint: A volume target; finish small challenges steadily.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: challenges presumably repeat or at least accumulate. What counts as a challenge is whatever the game’s own tracker says.
trophies.verification: Track completions in the relevant menu; the notification fires at fifty.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Shaking a four-star wanted level alongside your partner is a staged chaos exercise, and the atlas treats it as a planned stunt rather than an accident. Build the heat deliberately in a stretch where your partner is active, because improvising a four-star escape is where runs go wrong. Choose the getaway route and vehicle before the stars appear. The unlock lands when the heat fully clears.
steps: Raise a wanted level to four stars with your partner active
Plan an escape route and vehicle beforehand
Run the heat down until it clears
trophies.hint: Escalate deliberately, then escape with a planned route.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: the wanted system presumably works throughout free-roam. Whether the partner must survive to the very end is unverified; keep them alive as the natural reading.
trophies.verification: The wanted stars clearing while the partner is active, followed by the notification.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Three shop robberies on a live wanted level is a streak exercise, and the atlas plans it like a circuit: shops chosen for proximity, robberies triggered in sequence, heat deliberately kept alive between them. The failure mode is losing the wanted level accidentally, so route the run away from ambush-friendly streets. Plan the final escape to start immediately after the third shop. The streak ending is the unlock.
steps: Pick three shops close together
Trigger the robberies in sequence
Keep the wanted level alive until the third completes
trophies.hint: Three shops in a row, heat never cleared between.
trophies.missable: No missable risk identified: shop robberies presumably repeat. Whether the heat must still be live at the exact completion moment is unverified; keeping it hot continuously satisfies either reading.
trophies.verification: The third robbery completing with the streak intact, followed by the notification.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: One hundred discovered vehicles is a breadth trophy, and the atlas habit is simple: never take the same model twice when a new one is parked next to it. Common models fill the count early, and the real work is the rare tail, which deserves its own session with the in-game list open. Ride, drive or steal — the description only says discover, so prefer being behind the wheel when something unusual appears. The hundredth discovery fires the unlock.
steps: Vary every vehicle you take across the campaign
Check the discovery list periodically
